objective: Unblock a mechanically valid response from an independently unavailable auxiliary material-energy diagnostic, with explicit opt-in semantics and new numerical qualification.

observed_evidence.scope: Finite raw fields are observations only; complete public force entry still failed and no HP comparison ran.

actual_dependencies.finding: Auxiliary material-energy computation is not differentiated to obtain P or the weak residual. Its DD pair is nevertheless included in the combined support flag; _numpy_response rejects that flag, and _check_output requires every old returned field finite.

The explicit tangent uses residual size, retained F/J/Hu/delta and G pairs, branch selectors, operators and material coefficients; no material_energy input. Public tangent currently calls the full-field response first, so an energy failure blocks it upstream.

Mean constraint, fixed-force-scale Newton/Armijo merit, residual balance and accepted metrics use mechanical fields. Only output-spring energy appears as a separate finite algebraic metric; material_energy is not consumed.

Assembly calls the full-field force entry, then cached mechanical tangent. Accepted packages require material_energy in the current 17-field forces archive. Persistence schema/readers must explicitly reflect an omitted auxiliary field.
The existing supplied-state force result includes material_energy and its sum in metadata; it cannot silently become a mechanical-only result.
The result itself stores only tangent tensors/matrices, but its public base response still inherits the full energy gate.
Legacy unsplit accepted metrics explicitly require finite material_energy and report solid/medium sums. Keep that entry unchanged; do not route mechanical-only fields into it.

minimal_proposed_interface: Add one opt-in NumPy mechanical entry and corresponding assembler. Reuse unchanged stress, weak-force, kinematic and DD formulas. Do not compute the auxiliary energy branch when mechanical-only mode is selected.

Compute a named mechanical support flag from all required kinematic/coefficient/mechanical DD pairs, including inverse/log/exponential/action pairs; do not merely ignore or overwrite the old combined arithmetic_supported flag.
Keep existing complete-field NumPy/JAX entries, field sets, support bounds and error behavior unchanged. An explicit full/auxiliary request must retain the original energy requirements.

Mechanical-only fields omit material_energy. Record auxiliary_material_energy status=not_evaluated and qualified=false rather than synthesizing zero, replacing NaN, or pretending the old field is available.

Use an explicit new native mechanical force/path schema or entry. NativeMean cached arrays become an explicitly declared mechanical field set; metadata and pure saved readers distinguish availability. Reuse the existing controller/Armijo/KKT unchanged.
Reuse the cached mechanical response for _tangent. Preserve fixed-lift df/dw semantics, unsymmetrized full CSC and the qualified DD action consumer; do not switch to an energy Hessian.

next_verification.captured_state: Original full 3200-cell F16 split arrays and original 27-array model; no accepted-state or equilibrium claim.
next_verification.required: One newly evaluated complete mechanical force plus one cached tangent, three DD action consumer calls and fresh HP80/120 mechanical force/Jv comparisons on the declared full-domain witness.
next_verification.gates: Keep original total/component force and tangent-action limits, force/action floors, HP agreement gate, all element and DOF coverage, CSC storage checks and original CI bounds.
next_verification.regression: Existing meaningful focused tests plus bytewise unselected near/direct mechanical fields; confirm old full-field behavior and omitted-energy metadata explicitly. Avoid repeating prior unrelated whole-stage audits.
next_verification.scope_after_pass: Only this supplied F16 mechanical response and its declared directional action. No auxiliary-energy, T25, unloading path, equilibrium, contact/clamping or general-domain qualification.

open_decisions: Root chooses the precise opt-in entry/schema names before implementation. No numerical gate or old complete-field requirement is changed by this plan.
